title: The Manichaean Scriptures (article, AJSL 1920)
author: M. Sprengling
description: 'The Manichaean Scriptures' by Martin Sprengling, a short scholarly article published in The American Journal of Semitic Languages and Literatures (1920), now available as early journal content on JSTOR. Writing in the wake of the discoveries at Turfan in Chinese Turkestan, which had recovered Manichaean manuscripts in Middle Persian, Parthian, Sogdian, Old Turkish and Chinese, Sprengling discusses the canonical writings attributed to Mani, the third-century Persian prophet who founded Manichaeism, as described by ancient and medieval sources, and how the new finds of Manichaean hymns and texts were beginning to illuminate them. Manichaeism, a dualistic religion of light and darkness that spread from the Roman Empire to China, drew on Gnostic, Zoroastrian, Christian and Buddhist elements. It is a brief article rather than a book, included as a source on Manichaean literature.
